newsitem.title: CHINA: Sixteen Thais believed killed in China air crash.
newsitem.headline: Sixteen Thais believed killed in China air crash.

text.p: At least 16 Thais were believed to have been among 35 people killed when a China Southern Airlines Boeing 737-300 crashed while landing in the southern city of Shenzhen, a city government official said on Friday.
"From the figures we can calculate that at least 16 Thais are dead," the official said by telephone from Shenzhen.
Of 25 Thai tourists on the ill-fated flight from the southwestern city of Chongqing, only five had been found among 35 injured people, the official said.
Four passengers remain unaccounted for, meaning that at least 16 Thais appear to be among the dead, he said.

The three-year-old aircraft, carrying 65 passengers and nine crew, slammed into the tarmac during a thunderstorm at an airport in Shenzhen, broke up into three main pieces and burst into flames at about 9.30 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Thursday, officials said.
It was China's first big aviation disaster for almost three years.
